summary: FRP (Fire Radiative Power - Yangın Radyasyon Gücü)
details:
What it does / how it works
 Unified Fire Activity Calendar merges NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspots into one view. Users pick a 2023–2026 date range and region (or custom coordinates). Detections are matched within 1 km / ±6 h, then shown as a point map, activity chart, and FRP (Fire Radiative Power), with optional period comparison.

Benefits
 Cuts double-counting and sensor confusion; shows intensity (FRP), not just counts; makes year-to-year comparison fast; one public link for the whole team.

Intended impact
 Help fire managers, responders, and researchers answer “How bad is this season vs last year?” using open NASA Earth data—faster, clearer decisions for communities at risk.

Tools & languages
 Python, FastAPI, DuckDB/Parquet, HTML/JS, Leaflet, Chart.js, GitHub Pages. Data: NASA FIRMS Archive.

Creativity
 Turns two separate satellite streams into a single fire calendar with map + counts + energy (FRP) and one-click period compare—built to stay online as a lightweight public demo.

What we considered
 Open NASA data first; usable without huge downloads; map speed and readability; desktop + mobile; clear Space Apps demo story (live app + 10-slide pitch).
